entries.text: All 3D burrow, skeleton, X-ray, flood, and labeling visuals are illustrative reconstructions for storytelling, not real footage or direct observation of the ancient event.
The script refers to a rock/burrow cast containing two animals; the specific specimen identity, repository, and publication evidence must be verified before final publish.
The line states 'Two hundred fifty million years ago'; the precise geological age and dating basis must be verified against the primary source.
The animals are described as a mammal relative and an amphibian; exact taxonomic identification must be verified against the specimen/source record.
The amphibian ribs are described as healing with no bite marks; this anatomical/pathological observation requires primary-source verification before being stated as fact.
The interpretation 'not a hunt' is presented as an inference drawn from the stated absence of bite marks and healing evidence; it should not be framed as absolute certainty.
entries.basis: Inference stated in-script from reported injury pattern; depends on verified evidence for claim-healing-no-bites.

entries.text: The amphibian likely crawled into the burrow for shelter; this is a behavioral hypothesis/inference, not a directly observed event.
The mammal relative was probably in aestivation, a deep dormancy; this is presented as the most plausible interpretation and requires primary-source support.
A flood filled the burrow and sealed both animals; the burial mechanism is presented as a plausible story element pending source verification.
